Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, what does the visual evidence establish about the requested move of the source mug to the right of the headphones: complete fulfillment, partial progress, no progress, or unresolved?
node.criteria: Compare the source mug and its former location with the edited image, including all visible mugs and their positions relative to the same headphones. Pass only if evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself was moved and is now to the right of the headphones. Fail only if evidence reliably establishes that no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. Treat as partial progress when visual evidence supports an attempted or incomplete move of the source mug, such as a plausible remnant at its former location together with a mug on the right, but does not reliably establish that the source mug itself reached the right side; do not infer source-mug identity from a right-side mug alone. Use unknown when the evidence cannot reliably establish either relevant progress or no progress, or cannot determine whether the requested condition is fulfilled.
node.binding: Cross-image binding: the source blue mug and the same headphones in the source and edited images. Compare the source mug with all visible edited mugs, assess their left-to-right positions relative to the headphones, and inspect the source mug’s former location for evidence of a remnant or movement, allowing for changes in scale, lighting, and appearance.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows one blue mug to the left of the headphones. In the edited image, a mug is visible to the right of the headphones, but the source mug’s former left-side location contains a conspicuous blue, mug-shaped blur, and another mug appears left of the headphones. This does not reliably establish that the source mug itself was moved to the right; the visible evidence instead supports no relevant progress for the source mug, rather than fulfillment.

response.content: {"text":"The trace notices the key ambiguity but collapses it into “no progress”: the edited image shows a conspicuous blue, mug-shaped blur at the source mug’s former left position and a mug to the headphones’ right, which is evidence consistent with an attempted/incomplete move under the stated rubric. Do not treat uncertainty about whether the right-side mug is the same mug as proof of no progress; distinguish plausible movement/remnant evidence (partial) from reliable evidence of no change (no), and reserve unresolved for cases where neither can be established. Keep the source-object binding and inspect all mugs and the former location, but calibrate the decision to the rubric’s partial-progress criterion rather than requiring identity to be proven before recognizing progress. This is a visual classification disagreement, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure; the reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth."}
